reason: E1 directly supports the microstructural change to FCC+Laves and the associated hardness/strength increase for Nb5, but neither E1 nor E2 provides any evidence for in situ formation of a lubricious Nb-oxide tribolayer or its effect on friction and wear across the full temperature range; the tribological mechanism is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Nb doping (≈5 wt%) changes CoCrFeNi from single-phase FCC to dual-phase FCC+Laves
The dual-phase structure increases hardness and strength
Nb-enriched regions oxidize at high temperature to form a protective lubricious oxide layer
The oxide/tribolayer reduces friction and wear across 25–800 °C
